title: Terminal shoot maturity orchestrates Carbon–Nitrogen balance and hormonal signaling to regulate floral induction in litchi (Litchi chinensis Sonn.)
content:
by Qiusheng Xiao, Yuqing Niu, Xingjie Li, Fayong Li

Floral induction in litchi (Litchi chinensis Sonn.) is triggered by chilling but strictly contingent upon terminal shoot maturity; however, the regulatory mechanism linking shoot status to floral fate remains elusive. This study investigated the physiological and molecular determinants of flowering in ‘Feizixiao’ litchi shoots of varying maturity under natural winter chilling. We found that shoot maturity is a prerequisite for flowering competency. Mature shoots accumulated significantly higher carbohydrate reserves (soluble sugars and starch), resulting in a high carbon-to-nitrogen (C/N) ratio compared to immature shoots. Hormonal profiling revealed that maturation remodeled the hormonal landscape by upregulating abscisic acid (ABA) and suppressing gibberellin A3 (GA3). Expression analysis identified key flowering-regulatory genes, including promoters LcFT1 and LcSPL1 and repressors LcTFL1 and LcSPL6. Correlation and PCA analyses identified the high ABA/GA3 ratio and carbohydrate accumulation as intrinsic drivers activating the LcFT1-mediated pathway. These findings suggest that shoot maturation coordinates a favorable metabolic and hormonal environment to unlock the genetic program for floral induction, providing a theoretical basis for managing alternate bearing in litchi.
